violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: sliced ham (43-46F), sliced turkey (44F) in 1 door upright cooler on cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. Person in charge discarded items.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw fish stored above uncovered chocolate pudding and juice cups in 2 door upright cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Person in charge placed raw fish below all foods that are ready to eat.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cooked sausage patty (78F) covered with plastic wrap in 1 door upright cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Person in charge discarded sausage patties and trained staff on proper methods of cooling.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: baked rolls
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. PIC discarded rolls and trained all staff on proper glove use while handling ready to eat foods.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cooked beef patty (97F) in steam well.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. PIC reheated beef patties to 165F.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): storing breads off of the floor of walk in cooler and freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. PIC will provide dunnage racks or wire racks to increase storage capacity for coolers

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Surfaces of ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment are not being cleaned as required. The inside of the ice machine was visibly soiled and in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. EHS DISCUSSED CLEANING THE INTERIOR OF THE ICE MACHINE BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. The commercial sausage in the tall reach-in refrigerator was above 70F and cooling started more than 2 hours ago.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. The sausage patties were discarded.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling:the sausage was not being cooled properly. It was covered and stacked in the refrigerator. Use thinner layers and uncover foods while cooling.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. If there is room in the walk-in, it can be used for cooling.

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): storing items off the floor in the freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks.

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Air Gap Provided
violations.observation: Observed the pre-wash spray hose to extend below the flood rim level of the sink basin at the 3-vat sink.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by providing an air gap as specified under 5-202.13. The spray hose at the 3-vat sink shall be altered to hang above the flood level rim of the 3-vat sink in order to provide an air gap. The spray hose must be adjusted so there is a suitable air gap, or replaced. The food employee temporarily adjusted the height of the sprayer and the manager will get the hose properly adjusted or replaced.

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Covered Receptacle in Women's Toilet
violations.observation: There is no cover to the feminine napkin refuse container in the ladies room stall.
violations.corrective_action: A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. Vierra Falls Church (Inspection Date: 07/29/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Floors/Walls/Ceilings, Materials Smooth, Durable, Cleanable
violations.observation: Grout is missing from several areas on the kitchen floor. This is allowing water to pond and making it not easily cleanable.
violations.corrective_action: Wall, floor, and ceiling surfaces shall be smooth, durable, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, warewashing areas, and toilet rooms. Replace the missing grout.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Protective Shielding on Light Bulbs
violations.observation: Observed that the end caps are missing from the protective light covering of fluorescent light fixtures in the dry storage room
violations.corrective_action: Provide end caps to completely enclose the light bulb. Install the missing lightbulb shield, or install a rough service light bulb to protect foods and equipment in case the bulb breaks.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: tomato soup observed in 1 Dr upright refrigerator holding at 43-44F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC stated the refrigerator door is opened a lot during lunch service. PIC discarded the food. It is recommended to keep foods that are not being used for service in a different unit so they may stay cold at 41F or below.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed that portions of flooring tiles, wall tiling, and door framing is not maintained in good repair.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities. PIC stated there is a work order in place for the cracks seen at the top of back door frame. **Repair or replace tiling throughout kitchen to maintain a smooth and easily cleanable surface with no broken pieces.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: GROUND BEEF WAS THAWING ON DRAIN BOARD OF PREP SINK.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EHS DISCUSSED ABOUT THAWING METHODS WITH CFM. CFM RELOCATED THE GROUND BEEF TO WALK-IN COOLER.
